problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis $B={[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]}$ of ${R}^{2},$ find $[x]_{B}$ if $x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing the components of $x,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{6}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{6}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$
